cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Approve 'storage problem' for the newsletter, please. Our volunteer delivered the cake on time; I'm not letting her take the blame.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why not say we left it by the radiator?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Because a report needs the failure, not a tour of the room. 'Stored too warmly.' Can you approve that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: With 'full refund'. They paid for a cake they couldn't eat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Full refund promised or paid? Check before you sign. I'm trying to repair one mistake, not publish another.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 wants a newsletter explanation approved to protect a timely volunteer. A3 corrects B2's detail selection and A5 checks the exact claim implied by B4's refund condition.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 proposes naming the radiator; A3 recasts this as storage failure. B4 requires refund information, so A5 asks whether it is promised or already paid before signature.

relationship.evidence: B2 favors factual disclosure and B4 favors fairness to paying readers. A's professional editing answers both contributions while protecting the volunteer.

heightening.evidence: B4's repair proposal gives A5 another accuracy problem to supervise, extending the same superior editorial method rather than inventing another accident.

specificity.evidence: A1 locates newsletter approval after a cake delivery; B2 names warm storage and B4 says it was inedible. Those facts establish why the statement matters.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's tour-of-room dismissal and A5's publishing warning are directed at B's editorial choices; the ending contains a check and reason, not four separate moves.

coach2.stated: A1 says delivery was on time and seeks approval; B2 says they left the cake by a radiator; B4 says customers could not eat it and wants a refund mentioned.
coach2.inferred: A is protecting the volunteer and perhaps their own organization; no invented job title is needed for editorial supervision.
coach2.missing: Whether the refund is paid is intentionally asked at A5, not assumed.
coach2.firstDefect: No failed gate found; A5's unanswered question is the current task, not an unsupported premise.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 offers a more specific wording for A1's requested statement.

B2-A3.evidence: A3 rejects B2's level of detail and proposes a fault description.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 conditions approval of A3's wording on refund disclosure.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 asks B4 to verify the refund's status before signing that claim.
